recent_reviews.author: Bob Davies
recent_reviews.text: The next patients' group meeting is on the 6th of May at 5pm. We established that patients can arrive a little early (say 10 minutes) to discuss individual problems/experience, so the PPG can focus clearly on shared problems. Whether you can attend or not, please write your review, good or bad, and I will continue to bring them to the new team. From the PPG meeting on Feb 4th... The practice is fully staffed for doctors (now at 6, and 6 admin) but doesn't have a practice manager as they're having trouble recruiting because they will also manage the Oldham practice. I have been assured they're wiring up a better fallback after 2 missed calls (most likely you will receive a text that asks you to ring the practice, but I have asked that a bookable slot picker be added too). The website is now 24hr accessible for admin/repeats, but still cannot be used out of office hours to request an appointment. The doctor has concerns about people using it for 'urgent' requests in the middle of the night (when no doctor is available to receive it), I've tried to make a case for it, but if out of hours appointment-requests is a blocker for you, please come to meetings and help me argue the case. I have also reraised when tests come back all green, but you're still sick, the practice currently close your diagnosis process until you re-engage (which you may not be told you need to do), which I intend to reraise in future. --- From the PPG meeting on November 26th... 2 new doctors are on board, and new staff are coming soon. Complaints about reception seem to be improving, less reliance on agency staff. The website will be switched to 24hr accessible. New Bank is on Bookable, which is much easier to use and is currently accessible outside of office hours (unlike PATCHS), but doesn't work for existing registered patients, and only has a limited number of slots and is only for booking an appointment. --- From the PPG meeting on 10th of September. The practice is moving to a new digital system on 1st of October, which 'should' solve some of the current technical issues with arranging appointments. Management say there will be some onboarding help and open/group sessions for anybody who would like to attend, and dates/times of those will be on a notice-board in the reception (or from Lynne, the operations manager) once those dates are arranged (probably a couple of evenings/saturdays depending on demand). We have also been assurred the quality of help from reception has been better in the last month and will continue to improve. There is still no new practice manager. They are recruiting for one in a difficult market, but they are adding new administrators (from October 6th, if I understood correctly) and _should_ soon be adding extra doctors too, with a less clear timescale (presumably notice-period related). The patient load on doctors is within the normal NHS range, so do not put off making an appointment just because you think they're busy, they have capacity and are adding more, and most of the problems seem to be steadily improving. --- After leaving a previous 1 star review with many negative points and being frustrated with being unable to arrange an appointment, I attended the newly set-up Patient Participation Group meeting (as a new management company took over in April) on 6th August. The discussion between the team and a few patients was constructive and the new management team seem to have an understanding of the problems after we explained in some detail. I also brought these reviews to their attention, and provided a breakdown of reviews to their management in the meeting. If you're here because you've had a negative experience, either recently or before the take-over, we've been assured they're working on it and should be moving to a new system, as well as dealing with the problems caused by specific staff. Please contact management with feedback and come to the patient meeting if you have the time, be heard, the new team are (it seems) finally listening, and they actually have a mandate to fix problems atm.

recent_reviews.author: Ken Kamdy
recent_reviews.text: A call was initiated to ascertain why an appointment for a mother and child was declined by a GP, providing clinical advice to the service user, and you are not part of the medical team. NHS staff must not unreasonably deny access to services, and patients are entitled to be treated with dignity, receive clear information, and file a formal complaint regarding inadequate care or discourteous conduct. However, a staff member and a receptionist unjustly canceled an appointment, and I have requested the call log. Non-clinical reception staff should not act as if they are GPs; clinical decisions regarding whether a baby or parent requires a review should be made by a qualified health professional (GP, nurse, ANP) following appropriate triage protocols. Professional guidance underscores that healthcare professionals must not unreasonably refuse a patient access to care that addresses their needs and must communicate with kindness and clarity, particularly with vulnerable patients such as parents of very young children. A receptionist informing a practice or service user that she does not consult a GP also provides clinical advice to the service user. Merely asserting that a one-year-old “does not need to see a GP” without a proper clinical evaluation or justification is unlikely to adhere to good practice standards regarding communication and access to care. It is unfortunate that this matter is not being addressed; I intend to escalate this issue further due to the appalling service.

recent_reviews.author: Fiona Simpson
recent_reviews.text: I am always really happy with and satisfied with all interactions with the surgery, and actually recommend it to others. The 2 main doctors and advanced clinician are always very good and are through, listen and take concerns seriously. The patches system is very good and easy to use - myself and spouse have had to use it a few times recently, and we have always then been contacted with an appropriate appointment, if that was face to face, urgent phone, or routine that has always happened quickly. There are some people complaining about lack of appointments etc, I have never found this to be the case. I work in primary care and regularly deal with different GP surgeries, and believe me, simpson medical are one of the better ones!! Perhaps everyone needs to have realistic expectations, and consider that there is high demand for healthcare, which exceeds capacity. The old days of face to face appointments are gone, unless it is necessary this does not happen anymore - often phone calls, including photos etc are often sufficent, and more a more efficient use of staff resources. If a face to face appointment is necessary it will be made whilst anything regarding mental health has always been taking seriously and urgently. I am very happy with being a patient here, and think given the demand they do a good job, and are one of the better surgeries I deal with. Thank you to the staff, I appreciate it

recent_reviews.author: Junaid Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: As a long-term patient (diagnosed with a life time illness since 2005) receiving continuous prescriptions and specialized care, I requested a paid private letter confirming the simple, medically accepted fact that chronic stress and hardship trigger flare-ups to my condition. The practice refused the request, claiming "insufficient evidence" a shocking statement considering my two decades as a patient for whom they have continuously prescribed, medication, are informed of my hospital ongoing treatment for years (Vedolizumab, etc.) and liaised with the hospital IBD team. This refusal demonstrates a failure to understand the patient they are treating. Crucially, this contradiction occurred even though I attached an older letter from my specialist consultant where this clinical fact was already written and acknowledged. This extreme administrative obstacle wasted significant time and energy, forcing me to change GPs due to their unwillingness to support a chronic patient.

recent_reviews.author: JUNAID AHMED
recent_reviews.text: I was a long-term patient with multiple chronic conditions, including ulcerative colitis, arthritis, and migraines — all of which were regularly managed through prescriptions and hospital treatments. I requested a simple private letter confirming my diagnosis and how stress can affect my condition — something a hospital consultant had previously provided. Despite being willing to pay the £35 fee, the practice refused to provide the letter and didn’t offer an appointment to discuss it. As someone managing serious long-term health issues, I found this response dismissive and lacking in basic patient support. I’ve since moved to a new GP who I hope will be more patient-focused. I’m sharing this to help others understand what kind of support they might — or might not — receive here if they have complex or ongoing health needs. To the management: the decline in care became noticeable after COVID. If you’re genuinely reviewing patient experiences, it may be worth examining the internal changes made during and after the pandemic — because that’s when the ship started sinking.

recent_reviews.author: Hamaad Farooq
recent_reviews.text: I visited the surgery today while in severe pain and was told my prescription would be sent to the pharmacy. I went to the pharmacy but the prescription had not been sent. I returned after one hour and it was still not there. When I called the surgery, the receptionist told me to wait another hour while they checked with the doctor. When someone is in severe pain and unable to drive, delays like this are extremely frustrating and unacceptable. The doctor was kind and helpful, but the communication and urgency from reception staff needs serious improvement. What is also frustrating is that when staff are rude it seems to be accepted, but when a patient in severe pain becomes frustrated it is quickly labelled as “abuse.” Patients deserve to be treated with understanding and respect, especially when they are in pain and asking for urgent help.

recent_reviews.author: Philip Crossley
recent_reviews.text: Lottery appointment system, You need to call between 8am to 8:30am to win a appointment, but everyone else is also calling at the same time. If your call actually connects during this period, congratulations you have a ticket that gets you a 30% chance of an appointment ( providing they have not all been taken already) , if not try the lottery again the next day. You have 1/5 chance for an appointment if you follow my advice. I have a hack for those needing urgent doctor, use all the phones you can get access to and call them one after another, one will likely get through. Edit: It is possible now to go into the doctors before 8 am to obtain a golden ( yellow ) ticket, which helps you bypass the lottery phone system and be seen the same day. While the lottery system is not ideal, I can see its a way to deal with a already struggling health system and therefore I am rating this place higher for finding a way to deal with a failing system. (+2 stars )

recent_reviews.text: Dear Practice Manager, I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding the conduct of a receptionist during my calls to the surgery on 22/09/2025 at approximately 08:30am. During the call, I provided my son’s date of birth correctly ( date birth ). The receptionist repeatedly insisted that I had given the wrong date, despite me clarifying several times. This interaction became unnecessarily argumentative, and instead of acknowledging my clarification, she accused me of raising my voice, which was not the case. Feeling distressed, I called back and asked for my call to be transferred to another colleague who might better understand the situation. The same receptionist refused to transfer the call, insisting she had already corrected the date, which I found unacceptable and unprofessional. This is not the first time I have experienced rudeness from this particular staff member. As a parent of a young child, I expect to be treated with respect and professionalism when contacting the surgery, especially when the matter concerns my child’s health. I kindly request that this incident be investigated, that appropriate action be taken to address the receptionist’s behaviour, and that I receive a written response regarding the outcome of my complaint. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Sincerely and I will make this formal 100%

I am very grateful for the care and support he provided to my family.

recent_reviews.author: Faiz ul Haq
recent_reviews.text: I would like to leave negative feedback regarding Dr. Hussain’s behavior at this surgery. Whenever we ask him for medicine, even for our small children, he always responds by saying: “Go and pick it up from the shelf.” Most recently, my wife, who is pregnant, needed medicine. Whenever she calls, despite the language barrier, Dr. Hussain should at least try to understand that a patient is in need of proper medical advice and prescriptions. Instead, he simply tells her to “get it from the shelf.” I want to ask: if we always have to buy medicine directly from the shelf, then what is the point of having a doctor or a surgery? What role is he fulfilling? During the last call, my wife explained that the medicine he had prescribed previously did not help her at all. She requested an alternative. Instead of listening, Dr. Hussain told her she must not be using the medicine properly. My wife clearly said she knows how to take it, but it was ineffective. At that point, Dr. Hussain disconnected the call and again told her to “buy it from the shelf.” This behavior is extremely unprofessional, dismissive, and rude—especially towards a pregnant woman and parents with small children. A doctor should listen carefully, show empathy, and provide proper medical guidance. Unfortunately, Dr. Hussain’s attitude shows the opposite. I strongly believe that this kind of conduct is unacceptable within the NHS. If doctors are not willing to provide proper medical care and instead simply tell patients to “buy from the shelf,” then they are not fulfilling their responsibility as healthcare providers. I will also be submitting a formal complaint to the NHS regarding this matter. In my opinion, Dr. Hussain should consider retirement, as he does not treat patients with the respect, care, and professionalism that is expected from a doctor.

recent_reviews.author: Honey
recent_reviews.text: Awful experience this morning at this practice. First of all they thought the best time to do a fire drill would be with a full waiting room and in the freezing cold and rain. Then when we came inside which was 10 minutes after my appointment was meant to be I checked my nhs app to see that my appointment had been changed to 10:45 without my knowledge or notification. There was a reason I booked it at 10:20 not 10:45. I have also never experienced this in the past but I assume it’s so they meet their key performance metrics around access and availability. Some clarity on this would be good and do not blame the fire drill as it was nearly 10 after I should’ve had my appointment when the fire drill was done. Then the nurse I saw basically just fobbed me off when my condition hasn’t improved at all in a week. I have been told to wait another week and come back if it doesn’t improve despite already waiting before I came in to see someone in the first place.

Furthermore, my condition I've been visiting about causes me unbearable pain which the practice won't even prescribe pain killers for.Like Share Response from the owner a month agoDear Sydney Thank you for taking the time to provide feedback regarding your recent experience at the practice. I am sorry to hear about the distress and frustration this caused you and appreciate the opportunity to respond. My name is Lesley Hyde and I am the Practice Business Manager and part of my role is to monitor and investigate any concerns or complaints made to the practice. Please se below my response to the issues you have raised: Sample Collection Arrangements We apologise for the inconvenience caused when you attended the practice to drop off a sample at 6pm and were advised that it could not be accepted at that time. We understand how frustrating this must have been for you. For clarity, samples must be received by the practice by 4:00pm to ensure they can be included in the scheduled daily laboratory collection at 4:30pm. Samples received after this time cannot be accepted, as they may not be stored within the required conditions and timeframes set by the laboratory. Accepting samples outside of these parameters risks inaccurate or invalid results, which could affect patient care and safety. We do have a poster displayed in our reception area outlining the sample cut off time; however, we acknowledge your feedback that this information may not have been sufficiently visible prior to your visit. As a result of your comments, we have now placed additional signage on our front entrance door and updated our practice website to make sample submission times clearer and more accessible. You can view this update here: https://www.thearchmedicalpractice.co.uk/practice-information/sample-collection/ Our clinicians usually advise patients of the relevant sample drop off times when issuing sample pots. If this did not occur in your case, we sincerely apologise. We have reminded all clinical and reception staff of the importance of clearly communicating sample cut-off times to patients to help prevent similar situations in the future. Access to the Practice Building We are sorry that you felt unable to re-enter the practice and that this added to your distress. For staff safety reasons, when a receptionist is working alone at the front desk and their colleague is temporarily required elsewhere, the front door may be placed on a buzzer system. In these circumstances, patients are still able to gain access by pressing the buzzer and would be let in by a member of staff. We regret if this was not clear at the time and if it appeared that the practice was closed earlier than advertised. I can assure you however, the practice was still open. Pain Management and Ongoing Care We are sorry to hear about the level of pain you are experiencing. Prescribing decisions, including pain relief, are made by clinicians based on individual clinical assessment and current medical guidance to ensure patient safety. A GP would only prescribe “pain killers” if they felt there was a clinical indication to do so. If your symptoms are persisting, then I would encourage you to arrange a further appointment with a clinician so that your pain and ongoing symptoms can be reviewed again. Next Steps We take all feedback seriously and are grateful that you have brought these matters to our attention, which has already led to improvements in how we share information with patients. If you would like your concerns to be investigated further under the NHS complaints procedure, or if you wish to discuss my response further, please contact me at the practice (0161 226 0606). We are always looking for new members to join our PPG, if you would like further information of if you are interested in joining is, please click the below link: https://www.thearchmedicalpractice.co.uk/practice-information/patient-participation-group/ Yours faithfully Mrs Lesley Hyde Practice Business Manager

recent_reviews.author: Liv Zachariasen
recent_reviews.text: Keep dismissing me when I contact them when my toddler is poorly They just refer me to a pharmacy that I can't get to. If I want my toddler to be seen, I have to put through a complaint as it's the only way they'll take me seriously and the last time he turned out to have tonsilitis. My requests on AskmyGP just get closed off with a link to a pharmacy. I was never informed I'd have to be seen by a pharmacy first when I registered at this practice and it has never been communicated. They claim you'll be seen sooner, but before this we've always been sble to be seen on the day. I will never understand fobbing off parents who are worried about their small children and I get this every single time now. I have to always push to be seen and when they finally agree, I'm already so upset and stressed by the whole dismissiveness that I can't be bothered speaking to them. Not sure contacting a GP is supposed to trigger anxiety? It's more than reasonable to not rely on a pharmacy for diagnosis, especially for small children!! The last time he had a fever I didn't even bother contacting them as I couldn't be bothered with the thought of being fobbed off with a pharmacy referral. I get that the NHS is stretched and particularly GP practices, but you should be allowed a consultation every once in a while without a battle. I definitely hope nothing serious ever happens to myself or my family or we better hope the pharmacy can treat us. However having seen the pharmacist as they told me to, I'm none the wiser so what an absolute waste of people's time and energy to pass them round such a useless and inefficient circus. So disappointed as they have resorted to such a lazy way of dealing with their patients.

recent_reviews.text: Awful experience. Taken me off the database because I’ve moved from the area, even though I work 5 minutes away. I expressed that I would struggle changing gps because of underlying issues and they didn’t show any empathy. I expressed that my dentist etc were still in Manchester, as I am physically unavailable through the week to attend any appointments, working 6am until 8pm Monday to Friday. I stated that I’d had an ongoing condition, knew what it was but they had to test me. The first test they lost, the 2nd test they tested for the incorrect issue, the third they said I didn’t have what I thought. When I was referred to a specialist they confirmed on the day (within minutes of being tested) that I did in fact have what I initially thought! I believe if she wasn’t as strong as she was, just may have tried something unthinkable. When I sent a letter of complaint nothing was done. The doctors name is Dr Hoddes! They misdiagnose people, give them antibiotics or painkillers and they end up dying of cancer. Avoid at all costs!!!

recent_reviews.author: Oj B
recent_reviews.text: It's so heartbreaking to see this practice degenerate to this level. How hard can it be for people to be nice and professional? They have a lot to do in terms of training all their staff. And I mean ALL of them! From people's skills to civility, mannerisms, tone of voice when addressing patients and how to approach to patients who are already suffering. I've had so many unpleasant encounters with them that I don't want to mention. They make it look like they are doing a favour by attending to you. So appalling! They soon will be having no stars whatsoever if they don't make proper and needed adjustments on their people's skills. It really is appalling! Yelling at patients!! 9/03/2026 I can't believe that I am back here after 4 years to leave a very negative review of this establishment. Before, I go any further - I want to make it clear that, whatever issues patients are having with this medical centre are 90 to 95% front desk, admin, nurses and lesser staff (sorry, for lack of a better word to use.) The Dr's are unaware of the front desk, admin, and lesser staff issues - and yet bear the brunt of the end of the stick should the establishment suffer. I've had very unbelievable and excrutiatingly painful experiences with them from the beginning of this year. In short, (they put up lies and mark your profile, including your number should you call and then mete you undeserved shabby treatment by whoever picks your call, and for whatever reasons best known to them). From the tone of answering your call and how you are responded to is clear and obvious! It is like a syndicate in operation!!! Very evil and unprofessional!!! But we must continue to voice these issues until changes are made, and wrongs are righted. This afternoon I made a call to the centre, having moved to a new home, my daughter who had ran out of medication, due to pressure of moving into a new home and the process of registering with a near gp when settled; called Gorton Medical centre before the weekend to kindly ask for a repeat to be sent to the pharmacy for her to collect. It was not actioned. We called 111 for emergency prescription over the weekend. Today being Monday and on her last tablet, I called the pharmacy to ask if her prescription has come through from the gp, and they said it hadn't. I then called this medical centre to ask why my daughter's prescription had not been actioned and sent to the pharmacy since last week - Knowing she's been on same medication for several years and should not miss days? I was bluntly told by the reception to call back again,(of course, profile marking and syndicate operations in action.) I quickly reminded him how important her medication was, and he should please send it over to the pharmacy for collection. He said he was not in charge of that, and ended up pretending not to understand which medication was needed, (She's only on 1) and is in her profile. To cut the story short, I had no choice but to call 111 again. "Profile marking or spewed lies on the profile" was highly resonant in the voice at the end of the receiver too. I want to clearly state that these issues should be looked into by the right bodies in charge. People are being abused by those that should be providing care, and lives are lost due to these. (I nearly would have lost my life with this centre, cause i was refused care and gp appointment, and was bluntly told to do the worse I can not too long ago.) My daughter was refused duty of care, when she needed, and the excuse was, we had moved homes and was removed by the gp from their system- even when we had not yet registered with another gp. Where is the duty of care? What is the professionalism in this? This is gross misconduct and should be called out. And like I said in the beginning, Dr's are in consulting rooms doing their best and in very high cases are unaware of what goes on at the front desks, admins, and the rest. This types of evil must be called out and put away and far, please.

recent_reviews.author: Gavin Manchester
recent_reviews.text: Unwilling to make reasonable adjustments (due to learning disability) despite the Equality Act 2010 and The Autism Act 2009. Not a suitable surgery for neurodivergent adults (ADHD/autism) with long term lifelong mental health conditions or/and learning disability, not unless you have a parent/family friend to speak on your behalf, book and accompany you to appointments. Admin staff not understanding or particularly helpful and hold grudges/make assumptions, no training in autism/learning disability. (Even if the patient is on the NHS Learning Disability Register). On one occasion I had a local authority social worker attend an appointment with me as an advocate and to see the challenges I face accessing lawful care. Complain or raise concerns and get told “go elsewhere”. Not a particularly modern thinking practice. Very much the “you don’t look autistic” attitude and “go for a long walk outdoors” when facing a serious MH relapse/crisis. Seem to have the attitude that anything mental health related means you must see the CMHT only and if not under psychiatric care they won’t help you. They don’t feel the need to update medical records despite communication from medical consultants. No excuse for treating vulnerable patients so ineffectually or cruelly.

recent_reviews.author: Rose Carbone
recent_reviews.text: Dr Atherton was absolutely great - as always - however it’s the whole booking/reception where there seems to be difficulty & errors - this last apptmt was at least the 3rd time where I’d been given incorrect information. This time it was an error in phone apptmt/face to face apptmt. Id been told it was a phone apptmt - whereas in fact it was supposed to be a face to face one - so I was waiting by the phone at home & no call came. One before I’d been given the wrong month info - so when I turned up at the surgery - my date & time was right but for the wrong month. Prior to that I’d been given a date and time but just before the booked apptmt I received a message from the surgery to tell me I couldn't actually have that apptmt as it had been booked in incorrectly & had been given an ‘emergency’ slot as opposed to routine - I had booked it 3 wks in advance - so then had to wait a further 3/4 weeks to finally speak to a doctor. Like I said when you do manage to speak with a doctor/nurse at the Practice they are brilliant - however some of the booking/reception team do let it down & it becomes very frustrating - especially if you are concerned about an issue. There were further errors - in a similar area but I have bored myself with this already - I’m only writing this because I was asked to & also hope that it can lead to an improvement in the booking system.

recent_reviews.author: The 5 Brothers Squad
recent_reviews.text: Benchill Medical Centre is no longer the practice it used to be. All the old doctors are gone, and what’s left is a team that seems to have no urgency, no compassion, and no sense of responsibility. My 12-year-old son developed a serious issue with his eye — it was clearly getting worse — and we spent over two weeks trying to get him seen. I called multiple times, explained that his condition was deteriorating, and still we were ignored. When they finally responded, they didn’t even book an appointment — they just sent us to a pharmacy, where we received no help at all. This isn’t just poor service — this is gross negligence. They failed to provide proper medical care for a child in pain, and they didn’t even follow up. The delay has made things worse, and we’ve had to seek help elsewhere. No examination, no urgency, no care. This practice has changed for the worse — it is now unsafe and unreliable. If you value your family’s health, especially your children’s, I strongly advise you to go elsewhere.

recent_reviews.author: Amrit Kaur Swalley
recent_reviews.text: During my call, I was advised by reception staff that I should take my mother to the dental hospital instead. This advice appeared to be a medical decision, which I found concerning, as reception staff are not clinically qualified to make such determinations. I later spoke with the reception manager, who confirmed that reception staff are permitted to make these decisions. This is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about patient safety and appropriate triage procedures. In addition, I do not feel that my complaint was handled effectively or taken seriously. There was no reassurance, clear explanation, or appropriate escalation of my concerns. I believe further training is required for reception staff, particularly regarding the limits of their role and the importance of not making or influencing medical decisions. As a patient, I expect clinical advice to be given by a qualified healthcare professional. This matter is particularly concerning given the Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements, which state that patients must be treated safely, appropriately, and with clear clinical oversight. I trust that this issue will be reviewed promptly to ensure patients are not placed at risk in the future. Thank you

recent_reviews.author: Erandi Samaraweera
recent_reviews.text: ⚠️ Serious patient safety concerns – I strongly advise de-registering I am writing this review as both a medical doctor and a parent who has been genuinely fearful for their child’s safety while registered at Junction Surgery and Alkrington Surgery. Since registering in August 2025, I have experienced repeated safety and professionalism concerns. My child was once prescribed antibiotics without enough doses to complete the course and I was told that “missing a few doses won’t matter.” This is unsafe advice and only corrected after I insisted. My daughter had a persistent cough for several months and attended multiple times, yet no appropriate referral or timely investigations were arranged. When she later developed fever and blood-stained sputum, an out-of-hours GP was clearly concerned and requested urgent investigations. Despite this, our concerns were dismissed the following day, my child was not properly examined, and I was given incorrect medical information. False reassurance when a child is coughing up blood is unacceptable. When I later requested an urgent private ENT referral due to ongoing bleeding, I was asked to pay a fee during a highly distressing situation, despite previously being told such referrals were not chargeable. The supervising GP did not attend to assess my child in person. Overall, I felt unheard, disrespected, and unsafe. Based on my experience, I would strongly advise patients—especially parents of young children—to seriously consider de-registering and seeking care elsewhere. IF ANYONE NOT TRUSTING ME PLEASE READ THE REVIEWS IN OTHER WEBSITE AND CQC REPORT

recent_reviews.text: I have been going to this surgery for about 24 years, I had mixed service from Dr Anglin, but have had good treatment from Dr Lazin. I'm pleased Dr Anglin retired he never paid attention to hospital letters sent to him. Dr Lazin is consistent in his care, reads all hospital letters and will correct my repeat prescriptions with new medication without my input, and will change them if they become incorrect, by a telephone call alone. The building is not very wheelchair friendly for chairs with wider seats. I'm pretty sure children or smaller wheelchair users should be able to get through the doors. But my larger chair can't get through any internal doors, so I would be unable to evaluate the building if a fire occured.

recent_reviews.author: Paris Pinglaux
recent_reviews.text: I had a 6cm ovarian cyst burst, had internal bleeding, and needed a blood transfusion. I needed urgent surgery. I ended up in A&E - called the GP a day or so later relaying my very worrying symptoms and A&Es findings (projectile vomiting, diarrhoea, unable to keep food/water/tablets down, excruciating pelvic and full body pain, falling in and out of consciousness, blood in urine). A GP told me it was ‘nerves’, and gave no explanation as to why my symptoms suddenly increased tenfold. I was refused anti-sickness tablets many times while dealing with the unbearable nausea and vomiting, because they can become addictive apparently. The pain was unbelievable, I had to take the maximum dosage of cocodamol a day, and that barely touched the sides. Rather than showing concern for the severity of my pain, nausea, and other symptoms, conversations around pain medications became interrogations regarding addiction. I had a large cyst that needed to be removed urgently. They should have heard my symptoms and flagged them as concerning. They should have contacted my NHS surgeon with those concerns, urging them to bring the surgery date forward. They should have spotted the signs and symptoms of a ruptured cyst. Instead of trying to understand what could be happening to cause these very severe symptoms, they did nothing but minimise and ignore my concerns, while refusing me medications that were saving me from ending my life due to the constant, excruciating pain. What exactly are these doctors trained in? How could you be a trained doctor and miss the signs of an ovarian cyst rupture, especially considering my suspected endometriosis? I felt that something was seriously wrong despite this, so I pursued private surgery. If I did not have the means to do that, as many do not, I may not be here now. I could have gone into sepsis, I could have developed blood clots, and god knows what else. Not only that, I also had samples necessary for a referral to gastroenterology go missing three times in a row, which is just bloody odd. I am still in unbelievable amounts of pain, and have ongoing symptoms. I spoke to the practice manager yesterday. I wanted to try to explain how deeply traumatic all of this has been for me. According to her, I should have contacted my surgeon and asked for the surgery to be moved forward, not the GP. Like ???? I didn’t know I had a cyst! That is why I went to my GP for help, so that they could flag this as a potential emergency, justify my concerns, and potentially get my surgery moved forward or flagged as urgent. I am not a doctor, I went to my GP because I had no idea what was going on in my body, I was unbelievably ill, and scared. Is that not what you are supposed to do? However, my concerns were minimised, and I was made to feel dramatic. So, I just kept suffering until I could finally be booked in for a private laparoscopy. I explained that my dad (also at the same practice) has stage four cancer, and recently my brother passed away too, so my mental and physical health are very poor. She wouldn’t let me finish and responded very unprofessionally. I can’t remember her exact words, but it was something along the lines of ‘don’t start that’ or ‘don’t go there’ because her father passed away and she had been through a lot too. Honestly, I was gobsmacked, still am. I don’t understand why she thought it appropriate to respond like that. It is her job, that she is paid for, to be the practice manager. I hoped she would listen to my concerns and understand how negligent the practice had been, but I suppose that would be an admission of guilt. I am 24. I haven’t even managed to graduate university yet because of how much I have had to go through. All I want is to be healthy! I have been living a nightmare, and this practice has only made it harder. The doctors that work there traumatised me. If you do choose to join this practice, ask for doctor Nisha. She is truly lovely. The rest are incompetent.

recent_reviews.author: Helen Perlin
recent_reviews.text: I had a very distressing experience with Dr Tse Belmond and feel it is important to share this for transparency. I attended an appointment following a panic attack. As English is not my first language, I brought my partner for support. During the consultation, my partner was dismissed and interrupted, and I was pressured to speak despite being visibly distressed. I was prompted to discuss a traumatic experience, which caused me to become extremely upset. Throughout this, I was not offered reassurance or support, and the lack of empathy was noticeable. At a later appointment, I raised concerns about possible Autism and requested an assessment. This was met with a dismissive response, including laughing, and statements were made that Autism is rare in women and predominantly affects men. I found this response unprofessional and not in line with current understanding. I also have concerns about how suicidal thoughts I disclosed were recorded, as they were documented as “depressed mood – minor,” which did not reflect the seriousness of what was discussed. Overall, I left feeling unheard, belittled, and unsafe. I would not feel comfortable seeing this doctor again and would advise others to be cautious.

recent_reviews.author: Gaz W
recent_reviews.text: Lack of compassion. Lack of professionalism. Lack of empathy. Arrogance. Rudeness. Failing of DPA. Ignorance. This all starts at the reception area. The ladies normally treat their patients like dirt. Very unhelpful with a “tough*” kind of attitude. Every other practice seems to work fine and use common sense, not Silverdale. For some reason you can’t book an appt using the My GP app for Silverdale, but other practices... no problem. You can call after 9am at most practices and book an appt for a GP.... not Silverdale. The poor service then trickles down to the GPs. I feel rushed. I feel things are not explained clearly. I feel they are more interested in hitting targets than curing the sick. Of course it all depends on the GP. I feel some GPs don’t listen to your needs, ailments or feelings and make massive assumptions and with any reason can’t wait to fob you off to a physio or hospital. I have been visiting this practice ALL MY LIFE. It has declined steadily and then rapidly. So after ringing up to book an appt with my GP for a later date, I’ve now been told I need to ring at 8am tomorrow.... WHY??? What difference does it make? Not only was I told this, it’s the arrogance and unhelpful attitude from the jumped up receptionist that is making me seriously consider switch GP. I’d you’re not registered with a practice, don’t bother with this one. It’s very amateur from top to bottom and the care no longer exists towards patients. UPDATE: what a mess. They are changing their system now. I’m certain this joke of a practice is making it deliberately hard for patients to speak to someone or make an appt. They even send texts saying “you have an appt on 02/09 at 2pm, this could be a phone or face to face appt, please contact the surgery for clarification on which it is” - WHY NOT TELL US IN THE TEXT?!? My god, this surgery was better in the 80s before we had computers and apps. I don’t think I’ve seen my GP face to face for 5 years. Absolute joke. UPDATE: after being told Curtis the physio is off sick AGAIN, I was asked to call to rebook an appt. Rang up and said I can’t do the rest of today as going to work. The lady said the nurse will be informed and call me to make an alternate appt. I got the call “we have appointments free all day with a GP” she said, I explained that I’d already said I can’t do this. I did however say, I can make a u turn now and come and see you “oh, we are booked up till 10:30” - the lady literally just told me they had a full free day?!? I eventually settled on 12:30 the following day. My text comes through to say my appt is 4:30pm the following day?!? I’m now sat here at 5pm and still not been seen to. This practice is a farce. No doubt I will get the usual reply from the practice manager where she takes no accountability nor responsibility for how dreadful Silverdale has become.

recent_reviews.author: John
recent_reviews.text: Been with this practice for years it’s a mixed bag and a lot of the time it’s good but in this instance it’s bad. Currently have an infection, went in the other day test showed no infection but symptoms present. Tried to get another appointment for a doctor to call me and tell me I had to go elsewhere to be treated instead of any further tests or questions being asked. When I raised about treatment times of the other service and the infection complicating due to this I was told “just because it might take awhile to be treated doesn’t mean it’s not the right place to go” anyway if the infection does complicate or spread and I get sepsis or any other issues due to the GP refusing treatment against what it says on the NHS website I’ll be sure to file a claim for medical negligence.

recent_reviews.author: deborah browne
recent_reviews.text: Towards the end of last year, I witnessed what I can only describe as a master class in customer service. I was waiting to collect something, as I noted Michelle take over a phone call from a younger receptionist, it appeared to be a difficult phone call. I moved away and took a seat. I couldn’t hear the caller, but from the time it took, and response by Michelle, I could tell that it took a lot of patience and calmness. There was a lot of warmth and empathy, and when Michelle finished, she introduced me to the younger new receptionist. I said to her take it from me you are learning from one of the best, and from what i observed, that was a master class in customer service. I think we forget that the front line staff in any medical centre, whether it is on the phone or face to face, do an extremely good job, and are faced with a lot of difficulties along the way, and are blamed constantly for things that are beyond their control. I know the Limes staff well, and they are all really hardworking and caring individuals. Please remember they are all doing their jobs, to the best of their abilities, and going through the same pressures of everyday life, as every one of us.

recent_reviews.author: Tracey Fowler
recent_reviews.text: I, and all my family have been lucky enough to be a patient at Elliott Street Surgery for over 44 years, and the level of care we receive has always been outstanding. It has never failed to be anything less than 100%. I want to express my deepest gratitude to Dr Shah and the team for the outstanding care and support provided lately especially to my Mum following her recent operation when she fell downstairs and broke her Femur bone. When Mum was finally discharged to bed rest at home, from Hospital after a new days, she was complaining that the feet were sore I thought she could be developing bed sores, I called the Surgery at 5.00pm, and the next day at 9.00am a Nurse called to examine Mum when she put us at ease and luckily, it was not bed sores! A week later I was worried about Mum again as her good leg swelled extremely fast at the foot and doubled in size - so I called the Surgery and I was called back within 5 minutes to say the Practice was closing in 30 minutes but Dr Shah would personally visit Mum on his way home and he did within 40 minutes, the door bell rang and Dr Shah was stood waiting to see Mum – I initially thought she had a blood clot in her leg, Dr Shah thoroughly examined her for over 10 minutes and explained things to us in great depth, he explained the swelling could be just because she has had the operation and was bed bound and not able to walk and be mobile, that was one scenario or, it could be water retention and a few other scenarios were discussed too. Dr Shah advised he would send a Nurse to collect Mums bloods the next day to see what the bloods revealed if anything. The next day, sure as his word a nurse attended to see Mum – bloods were taken and sent off. The next day we were called that evening by Dr Shah to say the results had not come back yet and he would call us the next day. That evening a Locum GP Called and said the bloods were elevated and we needed to go for a scan an appointment was made for 2 days later. That day, Dr Shah called to discuss Mums blood results, and I explained what had happened. recent_reviews.author: Neil Shepherd
recent_reviews.text: Avoid this practice if at all possible. I have been registered with the practice for 13 years and initially all was great. Currently, every time I have to deal with them, something goes wrong causing stress and anxiety when help is needed most. I was sent to get bloods elsewhere and when I attended the appointment I was told that the surgery should have given me some paperwork which they hadn't. I called in on my way home and was told "of course you need paperwork" as though it was my fault. The text they sent confirming the appointment stated I didn't need any paperwork. I wasn't even aware what the test was for as there was no other contact. They recently put me on medication for high blood pressure. Initially, the "GP" I saw put me on a drug which caused my ankles to swell so I asked if it could be changed. Their remote clinical pharmacist changed the drug but when I read the leaflet, it stated that it shouldn't be taken by anyone on anti-fungal medication, which I am. Another drug was prescribed and sent to a different pharmacy. When I went to the pharmacy stated, they said they hadn't got the prescription as it had been sent to another pharmacy which was closed, so I was without the medication for 3 days. I have been sent another appointment with the clinical pharmacist for next week. The times don't fit around my work so I called in to ask for a later call and was refused. Dr Archer agreed I could have a flu jab due my lung condition. An appointment was made for this on the same day I went for a kidney function blood test and I was told I could have it at the same time. The phlebotomist was about to take bloods for a test she had already done about 4 weeks ago until I told her it was a kidney function test and informed her that I had been told that I could have a flu jab at the same time. Her response wasn't good, but suffice to say she didn't do it stating that she was thinking of retiring due to the stress that the admin team were putting her under. I went to reception and was told "no, you can't have a flu jab as you're not old enough". I really do think that this practice has gone downhill which is a great shame as I used to sing the praises of all the staff. I hope Dr Archer reads this and takes some action as some of the staff are rude, ignorant, uncaring and more importantly following unsafe practices. Not what you want from a GP surgery. I am quite willing to discuss things further with him if he wishes to call me. I am currently looking for another practice hoping things will be better there. In the meantime, if I can be bothered I am seriously thinking about contacting CQC. Avoid Avoid Avoid

recent_reviews.author: PC Mumble
recent_reviews.text: I am updating my review because after speaking to various friends who visit other GP surgeries across Trafford, I appear to be quite lucky with Washway Road. My friends have awful problems getting someone to pick up a phone, they're always number 20+ in the queue, they can't get an appointment. I rarely have to wait to speak to a receptionist, they have some lovely ones who answer the phones these days, very helpful. I have had some very pleasant experiences and interactions with both admin staff and GPs over the last 6 months so I actually cannot complain. The AskMyGP system seems to work well now they have changed it to logging a request between 8 and 10, it's no longer a race to get your request in before it closes/gets full. The on site pharmacist is very good, he can resolve a lot of medication queries so you don't have to wait to see a GP. ******* GPs do not take women's pain seriously. Was ignored and told that 3 periods in a month was absolutely nothing to worry about and was offered a flu jab instead. Completely uninterested so had to go private and seek a second opinion. Currently recovering from a total hysterectomy inc. ovaries and removal of severe stage 4 endometriosis. I also had Adenomyosis. When I wrote to advise them of this, they couldn't even be bothered acknowledging me. This practice has gone totally downhill in the last year or so. Utter disgrace. Edit - it's worth noting this same review was rejected by the NHS website 'because it includes a serious complaint about a specific practice'. So do not trust their NHS review score.

recent_reviews.author: Abigail Awoyeye
recent_reviews.text: I had a very distressing experience at Medlock Medical Practice. I arrived on time for my blood test and waited as instructed, while several patients who arrived after me were seen first. After over 20 minutes, I calmly approached reception to ask for reassurance, as I was worried I had been forgotten. I am currently receiving treatment for anxiety and depression. Instead of reassurance, I was spoken to harshly and repeatedly called “rude” in front of other patients. English is not my first language, and I believe there was a misunderstanding, but my attempt to explain was dismissed. I was left feeling humiliated and extremely distressed and broke down in tears during my appointment. I would strongly encourage the practice to provide staff with additional training in compassionate communication, mental health awareness, and supporting patients with language barriers. Healthcare settings should feel safe and supportive, especially for vulnerable patients. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

I'm still sitting there, watching people come in after me and being seen before me. I didn't want to leave the waiting are as I was on my own, just in case my name was called. 2 hours later (to which I think another patient may have informed the reception desk) I was still there. She asked me to the desk. To my knowledge I was booked in She told me I had been put down as a non attendee. Apologised, then said they had been having problems with the computer system. To which I said obviously not, its the person inputting/working the computer. As I had seen approximately 7-10 people arrive after me and go in before me. So to me that's not a computer error, its a human error. She said I would have to come back tomorrow. I said absolutely not as I work early mornings, and could the doctor see me now as he finishes his shift at 5pm (it was 4.50pm) absolute sham. Luckily, for them to basically save face, I imagine. The doctor said he would see me.Like Share

recent_reviews.text: I would give less for the stress and anxiety the surgery caused me, but it doesn't seem to let me. If you need care, there is no point going here. The reception staff are lovely however the doctors, nurse practitioner don't seem to care whatsoever ever. In January after a visit to the GP I was given incorrect medication. After the issue was no better I went back, I was told by the GP the 1st GP was wrong. They gave me different medication. After 2 days and getting worse. I presented yo A&E and was kept on for 5nights. Being told each step of the way the GP was wrong. I should have been referred to podiatry on the first visit. The second I should have been sent to hospital... If I followed their guidance any further, I could have lost toes/feet. After hospital admission, I was sensitive to the medication so rang the GP to change it. They advised that technically I don't need medication anymore as I have had a course. Without even seeing me. But I did. That was my treatment plan from my discharge from hospital. This surgery completely exasperate medical conditions unnecessarily. It's almost like doctors don't care anymore.

recent_reviews.text: I’ve recently joined New Islington Medical Practice as I started to take more responsibility for my health issues, which lingered over the years. I’ve had a 10/10 experience through every consultation and clinician I’ve encountered so far. The facilities are clean and modern, and the reception/back office staff have been very polite and prompt in responses. The new appointment booking system has been very efficient. Having many personal/professional experiences at other GP practices as a GP doctor myself - I have to say New Islington Medical Practice is by far one of the best that I’ve encountered within the region. The waiting times are optimal. I’ve had multiple health issues which have either been resolved or I am now receiving further support for. For sensitive issues, the clinicians are non-judgemental and empathetic in their approach which makes a huge difference. Kudos to Dee and management for their successes thus far and keep up the great work.

recent_reviews.text: I've been here for my whole life, I used to give 1 star but I do believe some aspects of the surgery have changed in recent years which is why I changed to a 3. Dr Heron I've struggled with for years due to past experiences and I will not see him, however in pregnancy he has been decent which shows he does take SOME things seriously and is willing to help. I thought the reception staff had improved over the last year or so however recently they have gone back downhill and are back to being the stereotypical NHS dragons on reception who refuse to help or even acknowledge you past 9.01am when the slots are full - I have even had a GP apologise for this! However it must be said that for me the real star of the show in primrose is Nurse Sharon! She is one of the most kind and compassionate people you could ever meet and I'm sure anyone who has ever crossed paths with her would agree!

recent_reviews.text: Unacceptable and impersonal service especially when using the Ask My GP website. If these requests are not seen by clinicians how can patients be confident that the staff who are triaging them are sufficiently medically trained to judge whether a patient needs advice/help from a GP. I was advised by way of an impersonal on line response to an Ask My GP request to contact a pharmacy. When I did this I was then asked if I had contacted 111. How many hoops do patients have to jump through to be able to get help? Left in pain with a possible infection. It makes one wonder when you read media reports of patients who have ended up with sepsis or worse whether this is the right approach; I don't think so.

recent_reviews.author: Dan
recent_reviews.text: If I could give 0 stars if I could. I was born in Urmston and was at Urmston Group Practice til late teenage years, moved around and came back and signed back up. It's not the same doctors surgery that we used to know and love on Church Road. The receptionists need to go on a humility and compassion training course because their actions or there lack of are directly affecting peoples health and mental health. The receptionists also like to try and It seems to be a common theme that one or two of the receptionists (not all) do not seem to have any level of care or sympathy towards their patients. They forced me into crisis because I missed a phone appointment at 18:30 when my appointment was supposed to be 14:45. Apparently they tried to call me twice but number was dead. I know this to be untrue because not only did I not get any notifications that they tried to call but I also have a voicemail as well and they could have left a message. So when I call the next day )which was a friday) to find out what's happened and if I was going to have an appointment then rather than the one that didn't happen the day before. I was met with the usual "you've got to make an appointment, you'll have to call on monday" Despite the fact it was mental health tablets that I needed a review on, for them to use a poor excuse of "it didn't go through" when my phone is connected to wifi calls as well. I was so upset after it all I just told the woman if they aren't going to take me seriously I'll do something serious for them to take notice. No call back, no duty of care, no safeguarding, no making sure I wasn't going to do anything stupid. NOTHING. Then I received a very SNOTTY letter from the practice basically telling me off for saying what I said to the receptionist without even acknowledging that had they of cared or done their jobs, I wouldn't have been in meltdown mode and said what I said. So off the back of that, I have sent a complaint to them TWICE about the whole disgrace of a situation and I have yet to hear from them. Not even an acknowledgement. This review is my last hope that they see this and reply to me because if they don't then I'm going to go above their heads as it's becoming a joke at this point. Business are expected to acknowledge a complaint within 3 days and set out within that acknowledgement a time frame of when I should hear back from them. It's been months.

recent_reviews.text: My family has been with the surgery since it opened in the 80s. Dr Noone expertly navigated the Medical anomalies of my Dad and now Dr Sarfraz and her team are skillfully dealing with these medical quirks I have unfortunately inherited. In 2023 I was very poorly with AF and Heart failure and the medication designed to deal with problematic heart beats actually appear to exacerbate these with me. For the last 18 months Dr Sarfraz and the Elms have patiently and professionally supported me, navigating me through what in my case is a .minefield of problems. They listen to what I say to them and worked with me to bring me back to a place of good health. Huge shout out and thank you

recent_reviews.author: vincent dean
recent_reviews.text: As someone with Autism, I don't enjoy Clarendon's surgery as a whole as I never feel like anyone actually cares, even the doctors, I'm just a ticket in a line to receive my pill, I've been trying to get an ADHD diagnosis, I've just completed the form and have spent 20 minutes going through my emails, looking on the website, which is just an organised mess, the contact us, doesn't even look like it has an email address, if I'm a low intelligence person fine, but the fact that your website is difficult to navigate to simply send an email is disgusting, I hope I'm just missing something simple, i can't even call in to book an appointment as it's done online, Clarendons is a prime example of how the NHS just makes it difficult to receive healthcare in the UK
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: vincent dean8 reviews2 months ago As someone with Autism, I don't enjoy Clarendon's surgery as a whole as I never feel like anyone actually cares, even the doctors, I'm just a ticket in a line to receive my pill, I've been trying to get an ADHD diagnosis, I've just completed the form and have spent 20 minutes going through my emails, looking on the website, which is just an organised mess, the contact us, doesn't even look like it has an email address, if I'm a low intelligence person fine, but the fact that your website is difficult to navigate to simply send an email is disgusting, I hope I'm just missing something simple, i can't even call in to book an appointment as it's done online, Clarendons is a prime example of how the NHS just makes it difficult to receive healthcare in the UKLike Share Response from the owner 2 months agoDear Mr Dean Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. We are genuinely sorry to hear how frustrating and upsetting your experience has felt. We recognise that navigating healthcare systems can be particularly challenging for patients who are neurodivergent, and feeling unheard or unsupported is never what we want for our patients. We are sorry if our website has been difficult to navigate. Our website is regularly reviewed by Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (GM ICB) to ensure it meets accessibility standards; however, we understand that “accessible” does not always mean easy to use for everyone. We are currently reviewing alternative website providers to see how we can further improve clarity, navigation, and ease of contact. All our Doctors appointment requests are triaged by a GP to ensure patients are directed to the most appropriate clinician based on clinical need. We encourage patients to use our online consultation forms where possible, as these go directly to the duty doctor and support timely responses. However, online access is not the only option. Patients who are unable to, or prefer not to, submit requests online can telephone the practice, where a receptionist will complete the form on their behalf, or attend the surgery in person to receive support face to face. Please note that our phone lines are extremely busy, and waiting times inevitably increase when reception staff are assisting patients with completing forms, but this support remains available. All triage requests are reviewed and responded to within 24 hours via the contact method chosen by the patient. With regard to ADHD referrals, the specialist service is unable to accept referrals without a completed screening questionnaire being returned, as this is a requirement of the service. There is usually an option to return the completed form via an available link included in the accompanying text message, (valid for five days). We do however, appreciate the difficulty you have described and have taken this feedback on board. Going forward, we will also ensure that a return email address is clearly included within the message to provide an alternative way of responding. If you need further help or would like to discuss your concerns in more detail, our Reception Manager would be happy to assist and can be contacted via the surgery. We also have a dedicated Care Coordinator who can also support patients who need additional help accessing our systems. We also have an active Patient Participation Group (PPG), which meet regularly to share feedback, discuss patient experiences, and explore ways we can improve our services. We would welcome your engagement, and the Reception Manager can provide further information or help you get involved if this is something you would like to pursue. Thank you again for taking the time to share your experience. Your feedback is important to us and helps us continue to improve the care we provide.

recent_reviews.author: Humairaa Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: Had an appointment today at 11:40 for an ultrasound scan which I had to have a full bladder for. I took a taxi to the place but as the taxi driver went the wrong way, by the time I got through to the centre was 11:43 and I explained to the receptionist that I’ll be 5 minutes. She said that was fine. I arrived at 11:50 and sat in the waiting area waiting for my ultrasound. When I arrived, was only 1 woman I saw go in and come out 10 minutes later. After that it was just me sitting there waiting. Nearly 20 minutes had gone by so I ask the receptionist. She said I am half an hour late and how I said I’ll be 5 minutes and that they won’t see me , even though I walked in passed reception at 11:50 to sit in the waiting area which was by the ultrasound scan room. I explained myself. Then she said okay just continue waiting. 25 minutes later the person at the ultrasound came out for me and explained how I’m too late and she can’t fit me in. Even though I’m the only one there and have been for the past 35 minutes. She said she’s been calling for me. No one called for me at all whilst I was there. Whatever I was telling her wasn’t going through to her at all. So after sitting there for nearly 45 minutes on a full bladder that I’ve had for 2 hours, I got sent home and a phone call after to re arrange. No thanks I would rather not have the scan anymore to find the issue of what’s making me ill rather than dealing with people like this. And bare in mind whilst I was waiting, one woman kept coming in and out of the room ‘checking around’ but never called my name or spoke to me. Wish I could give this place 0 stars

recent_reviews.author: sophie butler
recent_reviews.text: Where to start? Half of the doctors don't listen, are rude, belittling and sexist and will just laugh at your problems or refuse to make referrals even if they can't treat you. If you want names- Dr Lyburn is extremely rude, condescending and just generally vile. Dr Badesha literally laughed at me over my skin problems. All the good doctors like Dr Ash seem to leave the practice. Most of the receptionist staff are extremely rude, then do their best to block you from making complaints. One of them tried to force me to give a personal reason for my visit to the GP and when I refused, I was refused an appointment. I was then gaslit by two reception staff over what happened. But I know for a fact phone calls are recorded so maybe they should start listening back to them if there is any confusion in their minds about what has happened. The practice constantly mess me around with my medication, saying they haven't received emails from my mental health team when they have clearly been sent. I have been left without medication and left on too low of a dose because of this. I will say the nurses are lovely and I don't take issue with any of them but unfortunately this isn't enough for me to stay at Sorrel Bank. Please find a different doctors practice if you are considering registering with this one, it's not worth it. I will be making a huge complaint about my treatment and then moving my whole family to a different GP practice. Edit: you will be able to see that the practice reponded to me suggesting I arrange an appointment with the practice manager. I did this. Practice manager did not bother to respond

I had never heard of this rule before, and it was not communicated clearly beforehand. We were only referred to this clinic because our original GP had no availability, and the experience was extremely disappointing. I felt there was a lack of flexibility and compassion, especially towards a sick child. I would not recommend this clinic to parents or anyone who might require understanding and timely care.

recent_reviews.text: I am disappointed with the level of service I have received from Mocha Parade Medical Practice. I visited their center to get registered when I first arrived in the UK, and they promised to get back to me in a few days. However, I did not hear from them after two weeks, so I reached out to them. They said that they could not find my records and asked me to register again. I did so, but I still did not hear back from them after another two to three weeks. When I contacted them again, they said that my records had been misplaced. I then submitted my records online, but it has been almost three months and I have still not heard back from them. I am concerned about the level of care I will receive if I need medical attention from this practice. I am also disappointed with the lack of communication and the apparent negligence of the staff. I would not recommend this practice to anyone.

recent_reviews.author: Eugene Friday
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely ridiculous experience. Unprofessional staff. Arrived 10 mins early for my appoitment which was supposed to be 10:40 am, only to discover that their free parking was completely full, forcing me to find a paid parking elsewhere. I paid for 30 mins until 11:05 am but I wasn't called in the given timeframe. Thus, I had to extend my parking. I immediately informed the receptionist and asked them to let the doctor know that I needed extra few minutes to extend my parking. But they dismissed my notice and informed the receptionist that they wouldn't wait and asked to book a new appointment. Instead of showing basic courtesy, they just refused to wait extra couple of minutes, despite the fact that they were 25 mins running behind. So somehow it's acceptable for them to be late but the patients get penalised for circumstances entirely out of their control. If you expect punctuality, maybe start by managing your schedule and facilities properly. I won't be returning and wouldn't recommend this medical practice to anyone.

recent_reviews.author: ENGLISH WITH SABBIR
recent_reviews.text: Terrible Experience at NHS GP Practice The Absolute Worst I am writing this review to express my extreme dissatisfaction with Dr. Parkin's NHS GP practice. This practice is, without a doubt, the worst healthcare experience I've ever had. Here's a list of my grievances: Unbelievably Long Wait Times: Getting an appointment is a nightmare. Even after securing one, expect to wait in the waiting room. Unprofessional Doctors: I've had appointments with various doctors , and none have instilled confidence. They seem unconcerned about my health problems. I would recommend looking for alternative GP practices in the area. There must be better options out there with qualified professionals who genuinely care about their patients' well-being. If you're looking for a GP experience that will leave you feeling more unwell than when you arrived, then NHS is the place for you! Buckle up, because this is a tale of woe. Getting There is an Odyssey: Firstly, reaching a human to book an appointment is an act of pure masochism. The phone lines are permanently engaged in a game of dial tone torture, and the online system is about as user-friendly as a medieval trebuchet. Finally, you're ushered into the office. Prepare for a five-minute consultation. Don't expect in-depth examinations or thoughtful diagnoses. Here, a generic prescription pad are your only companions. I understand that the NHS is under a lot of strain, but that doesn't excuse the unprofessional and unacceptable service.

recent_reviews.author: Amelia A
recent_reviews.text: I brought my daughter for an appointment and we were kept waiting 30 minutes past our scheduled time. When we were finally called in, we were then left to stand in silence for another 5 minutes while doctor Hassan typed notes from previous patients. While still typing and without making eye contact or examining my daughter, he asked why we were there. When I explained it was for a spot on her leg and that she’d had it for a few months, he immediately made a judgment and said it “must not be much of an issue” if we’d waited that long. He also commented that “they will ask why you haven’t brought her in for months” without explaining who “they” were, and before he had even looked at the spot. Only after making these remarks did he finally examine her leg and then told us it wasn’t serious and to return in two weeks with warm compresses. My concern isn’t the medical advice itself it’s the rude, dismissive, and judgmental manner, particularly when speaking to a parent about their child. Unfortunately, this is not an isolated experience. We have experienced similar rudeness from this doctor on multiple occasions. Between the repeated unprofessional behaviour, poor communication, and lack of respect for patients’ time, this is not a practice I feel comfortable bringing my children to, and I would not recommend it to other parents.

recent_reviews.author: L B
recent_reviews.text: GP's and Nurses are brilliant. Always friendly and easy to talk to. Both nurses I've seen there have been bubbly, happy and chatty and put me at ease, even when having a cervical screening :') One of the reception staff comes across very rude on the phone at times which isn't great when you're ringing up about mental health issues. She has at other times when I've physically been in the surgery been fantastic and extremely helpful. I can sympathise with them to an extent as they must get a lot of abuse but it shouldn't be pushed onto others. When you're physically in the building though they're all spot on. Struggle to get through and get appointments if you don't keep trying to ring at 08:00. They do seem to have introduced a phone queuing system which helps massively. With there only being a limited amount of appointments I think the reception staff need to be firmer in turning time wasters away and directing them to the correct place (pharmacy/a&e/self care). Also, they should tell people who repeatedly don't attend their appointments and dont have the decency to advise reception they will be struck off if they don't have a valid reason. Surgery is bright, airy and clean. Chairs could do with being spread out a bit more in my opinion but I'm claustrophobic so perhaps a bit biased. Overall, best doctors surgery I've been too in Heywood and I would recommend. All surgeries seem equally difficult to get appointments so can't hold that against them. As for the occasionally rude receptionist, this is just my experience and how I perceive something that's been said and that will differ from person to person. We all have bad days, we're only human :)

She has at other times when I've physically been in the surgery been fantastic and extremely helpful. I can sympathise with them to an extent as they must get a lot of abuse but it shouldn't be pushed onto others. When you're physically in the building though they're all spot on. Struggle to get through and get appointments if you don't keep trying to ring at 08:00. They do seem to have introduced a phone queuing system which helps massively. With there only being a limited amount of appointments I think the reception staff need to be firmer in turning time wasters away and directing them to the correct place (pharmacy/a&e/self care). Also, they should tell people who repeatedly don't attend their appointments and dont have the decency to advise reception they will be struck off if they don't have a valid reason. Surgery is bright, airy and clean. Chairs could do with being spread out a bit more in my opinion but I'm claustrophobic so perhaps a bit biased. Overall, best doctors surgery I've been too in Heywood and I would recommend. All surgeries seem equally difficult to get appointments so can't hold that against them. As for the occasionally rude receptionist, this is just my experience and how I perceive something that's been said and that will differ from person to person. We all have bad days, we're only human :)Like Share

recent_reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed with the standard of care I have received from this surgery. recent_reviews.author: Martha Beatriz Potter
recent_reviews.text: I'm writing this review as a frustrated patient who's had a shocking experience with this practice's service. I phoned at 8am and waited 25-30 minutes just to get an answer. I explained my situation - my consultant had asked them to prescribe more antibiotics for my lung disease, which makes any cold or flu linger and often leads to infections, making me cough uncontrollably and causing incontinence. It's a nightmare. The response seemed straightforward when I spoke to them, but then I got a call an hour later saying I needed to fill in an online form to be triaged. A nice lady helped me with this, but then... nothing. I phoned again at 2pm, was told they'd contact me, and... crickets. It's now 6:47pm. The worst part? This isn't the first time this has happened. I've ended up in A&E twice because their system is so appalling, and both times I've been told "this is something the GP deals with". I rarely use their service, but when I do, it's usually to be told to go to A&E or a walk-in centre. It's infuriating. To anyone considering using this practice, be warned: their system is broken, and it might end up costing you a trip to hospital. Not exactly what you want when you're already feeling well.

recent_reviews.author: Barry
recent_reviews.text: Having recently had a medical issue whilst abroad I was advised to contact my Medical Practice at home. I have been a patient at Greenbank since the 1960s fortunately I have not had to attend on a regular basis however I was pleased to be given a prompt appointment and saw a doctor who was most pleasant and professional and was able to fully interpret the advice I had received whilst abroad. She arranged for me to have an ECG which was done within a week at Greenbank by an equally pleasant and professional person. The results of the ECG were conveyed to me later that day by the the doctor who saw me initiallly and she organised for me to see a specialist at Oldham Hospital within days. I remember that a few years ago I read in the local paper a review of the Greenbank Practice which was rather poor, however after contacting Greenbank I was given the opportunity, a few weeks later, to meet with the leader of the group who had produced that report which illustrated how easy it is to criticise particularly over petty issues. The second follow up report a few months later recognised the true value of the Greenbank practice and the practice was marked up as Good. I have also had recent visits to see the physio at Greenbank with my slight hip problem and again I received prompt and professional help. My golf is just as bad however my hip is on the mend.
